Colonialism

/kuh-LOH-nee-uh-liz-um/ - the stress falls on LOH · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Colonialism means the practice of one nation ruling foreign territories and exploiting their resources.

Under colonialism, the island's schools taught children the geography of a country most of them would never see, while their own rivers went unnamed in the textbooks.

Worked Example

The spice warehouses on the quay, the governor's mansion on the hill, the railway running only from the mines to the port — the town's whole layout is a diagram of colonialism, built to move wealth outward.

Colonialism is more specific than 'conquest' or 'empire': conquest names the military event, while colonialism names the ongoing system that follows — foreign rule that settles in, runs the institutions, and channels the wealth home.

How Colonialism Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

conquest

conquest: the military taking itself — the event, not the ongoing system of rule

domination

domination: control by the strongest party, with or without settlement and extraction

Antonyms

independence

independence: a nation governing itself

self-rule

self-rule: government by the governed themselves

How Strong Is It? — influence → domination → colonialism

influence vs. colonialism

influence vs. colonialism: Influence over another country is far milder than colonialism — advice, trade, and pressure, with the other nation still steering itself.

domination vs. colonialism

domination vs. colonialism: Domination is weaker than colonialism — one power looms over another, but colonialism adds the full apparatus: foreign governors, foreign courts, and wealth shipped steadily away.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of colonialism.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — coloni

Root — coloni: settler, settlement (Latin colonus, a farmer-settler)

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: relating to

Suffix — -ism

Suffix — -ism: a system or practice

Put it together

Put it together: Coloni (settler) + -al (relating to) + -ism (a system or practice) = the system of planting settlers. Latin colonus was a farmer sent to till new ground; colonialism turns that single settler into a machine — whole administrations planted abroad to farm not just the land but the wealth of the people already living there.

Use the root in a new word: colony

Use the root in a new word: colony: The ants established a colony under the porch, a whole settlement of workers building tunnels through the summer.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / historical

Colonialism is the historian's and journalist's word for the whole system — rule, settlement, and extraction together. Use conquest for the military event and empire for the power that runs the system; colonialism names the practice itself and almost always carries moral criticism. Its unit-mates annex and subjugate name the system's two first moves: annexing the land and subjugating its people.
